answer: Separate batch and speed paths (Lambda) have two code paths. Correctness comes from the batch overwrite, reprocessing means rerunning the batch job, and the serving layer merges the two views at the boundary hour, so drift between layers is a standing risk. A single job definition that runs bounded or unbounded (converged/Kappa) has one code path. Correctness comes from handling late data in the stream, reprocessing is a replay of the retained log through the same job, and there is one output table with no merge. Replay needs enough log retention, and replayed emissions can duplicate in the sink, so use an upsert sink, a transactional sink, or a dedupe view.
